topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: These remarks introduce the final lecture and outline the core learning objectives regarding cancer therapy modalities.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the principles, therapeutic mechanisms, systemic toxicities, and drug resistance issues associated with traditional surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy.

topics.label: Exploiting tumor-specific defects and synthetic lethality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapeutic strategies designed to exploit distinct biological vulnerabilities of cancer cells, including hormone signaling dependence, cell cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and DNA repair defects.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibition and mechanisms of drug resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how hyperactivated oncogenic kinases are targeted with small-molecule inhibitors and detail the subsequent emergence of resistance via gatekeeper mutations, bypass signaling, and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the application of therapeutic monoclonal antibodies to disrupt receptor signaling, recruit immune effector functions, and deliver targeted cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer immunology and T-cell-directed immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the evidence for host immune surveillance against tumors and the implementation of immunotherapies, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific engagers, and CAR T-cell therapy.

topics.label: Clinical progress, challenges, and future therapeutic paradigms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize broad perspectives on historical improvements in cancer survival, the persistence of tumor heterogeneity, and the practical dilemmas surrounding clinical trials and future cancer management.
